rows.mechanismEn: Arab Spring protests destabilized government, creating conditions for civil war
War escalation forced CBY relocation to Aden, creating dual banking system
Dual central banks caused currency fragmentation and exchange rate collapse
Currency collapse reduced purchasing power, triggering humanitarian crisis
War disrupted banking operations, leading to sector fragmentation
COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated existing humanitarian crisis
Truce provided temporary stability but banking crisis persisted
Banking crisis reduced access to financial services, worsening poverty
Dual central bank systems created separate monetary policies, leading to divergent exchange rates as Aden printed new currency while Sana'a controlled old notes
Currency ban deepened monetary fragmentation, accelerating exchange rate divergence between Aden and Sana'a zones
Coalition military intervention led to port blockades, airstrikes on infrastructure, and economic collapse, triggering massive humanitarian crisis
COVID-19 oil price collapse eliminated Yemen's minimal oil revenue, devastating government finances and accelerating poverty crisis

The 2018 $2B deposit provided critical currency support and stabilized the exchange rate, demonstrating its effectiveness. This success led Saudi Arabia to extend the deposit in 2022 to maintain continued stability.

The 2018 deposit established Saudi Arabia as the primary bilateral financial supporter of Yemen. This precedent and the demonstrated impact of financial support led to continued and expanded support packages including the $500M in 2024.

The World Bank 2010 Social Fund project demonstrated the effectiveness of community-driven development and social protection programs. This successful model informed the design of the 2025 Financial Inclusion project, which also focuses on grassroots impact.
